meta.how_to_read: Technologies whose ring is not a matter of opinion. 'basis' says why: lifecycle = the vendor or maintainers ended support (Hold); ubiquity = measurable, universal and actively maintained use (Adopt); formal = the technology sits on a public maturity ladder, mapped Graduated -> Adopt, Incubating -> Trial, Sandbox -> Assess, Archived -> Hold (CNCF project levels); consensus = the practice is standard everywhere. Each item has a 'check' that run_gold.py --verify re-tests against live sources. Trial and Assess can only be certain relative to a stated rubric, so they use the CNCF ladder; to test against bbv's own radar, add its entries with basis 'bbv'.

items.name: Python 2
items.what: The Python 2 language line; 2.7 was the last release.
items.fact: Python 2.7 reached end of life on 2020-01-01 and gets no more security fixes.

items.name: AngularJS
items.what: The first Angular framework (1.x), not the modern Angular.
items.fact: AngularJS 1.x reached end of life on 2021-12-31 and its GitHub repository is archived.

items.name: TSLint
items.what: A linter for TypeScript, replaced by ESLint.
items.fact: TSLint was deprecated in 2019 in favour of ESLint and its GitHub repository is archived.

items.name: Xamarin.Forms
items.what: A cross-platform .NET UI framework, replaced by .NET MAUI.
items.fact: Microsoft ended support for Xamarin, including Xamarin.Forms, on 2024-05-01; .NET MAUI replaces it. The GitHub repository is archived.

items.name: PhoneGap
items.what: A framework for building mobile apps with web technology, discontinued by Adobe.
items.fact: Adobe ended PhoneGap in 2020 and the PhoneGap command line repository is archived.

items.name: Internet Explorer 11
items.what: Microsoft's legacy web browser.
items.fact: Microsoft ended support for the Internet Explorer 11 desktop application in June 2022 (endoflife.date lists 2022-06-14).

items.name: Adobe Flash Player
items.what: A browser plug-in for animations and web applications.
items.fact: Adobe stopped supporting Flash Player on 2020-12-31 and blocked Flash content from running from January 2021.

items.name: Microsoft Silverlight
items.what: A browser plug-in for rich internet applications.
items.fact: Microsoft ended support for Silverlight on 2021-10-12.

items.name: Linux
items.what: The open-source operating system kernel.
items.fact: Every system on the TOP500 supercomputer list has run Linux since November 2017, and the kernel repository is pushed to daily.

items.name: Git
items.what: The distributed version control system.
items.fact: The dominant version control system; the git/git repository has over 60,000 stars and is pushed to daily.

items.name: PostgreSQL
items.what: The open-source relational database.
items.fact: The official PostgreSQL Docker image has over 11 billion pulls.

items.name: Python
items.what: The Python 3 programming language.
items.fact: The official Python Docker image has over 9 billion pulls and the CPython repository is pushed to daily.

items.name: Kubernetes
items.what: The container orchestration platform.
items.fact: A CNCF graduated project since 2018-03-06, the highest maturity level.

items.name: Prometheus
items.what: The monitoring system and time series database.
items.fact: A CNCF graduated project since 2018-08-09, the highest maturity level.

items.name: TypeScript
items.what: JavaScript with static types.
items.fact: The typescript npm package has over a billion downloads a month.

items.name: React
items.what: The JavaScript library for building user interfaces.
items.fact: The react npm package has over 700 million downloads a month.

items.name: Continuous integration
items.what: Merging everyone's work into a shared mainline several times a day, checked by an automated build and tests.
items.fact: Standard practice, built into every major delivery platform (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Azure DevOps) and described by Martin Fowler since 2000.

items.name: Backstage
items.what: An open platform for building developer portals.
items.fact: A CNCF incubating project since 2022-03-15: proven by several adopters, not yet graduated.

items.name: Thanos
items.what: A highly available Prometheus setup with long-term storage.
items.fact: A CNCF incubating project since 2020-08-19: proven by several adopters, not yet graduated.

items.name: KubeVirt
items.what: Runs virtual machines on Kubernetes.
items.fact: A CNCF incubating project since 2022-04-19: proven by several adopters, not yet graduated.

items.name: Strimzi
items.what: Runs Apache Kafka on Kubernetes.
items.fact: A CNCF incubating project since 2024-02-08: proven by several adopters, not yet graduated.

items.name: Longhorn
items.what: Cloud-native distributed block storage for Kubernetes.
items.fact: A CNCF incubating project since 2021-11-04: proven by several adopters, not yet graduated.

items.name: OpenFeature
items.what: An open standard API for feature flags.
items.fact: A CNCF incubating project since 2023-11-21: proven by several adopters, not yet graduated.

items.name: Headlamp
items.what: An extensible web UI for Kubernetes.
items.fact: A CNCF sandbox project since 2023-05-17: early stage, worth a spike.

items.name: Kepler
items.what: Estimates the energy use of Kubernetes workloads.
items.fact: A CNCF sandbox project since 2023-05-17: early stage, worth a spike.

items.name: Inspektor Gadget
items.what: eBPF based tools to debug and inspect Kubernetes.
items.fact: A CNCF sandbox project since 2023-03-07: early stage, worth a spike.

items.name: Kubewarden
items.what: A Kubernetes policy engine that runs policies as WebAssembly.
items.fact: A CNCF sandbox project since 2022-06-17: early stage, worth a spike.

items.name: Tinkerbell
items.what: A bare metal provisioning engine.
items.fact: A CNCF sandbox project since 2020-11-10: early stage, worth a spike.

items.name: Akri
items.what: Exposes edge devices as Kubernetes resources.
items.fact: A CNCF sandbox project since 2021-09-14: early stage, worth a spike.
